easy.def: A soft, sweet candy made of sugar, butter and milk.
examples: I ate fudge.
The fudge is chocolate.
Mom made fudge.

more.def: A soft, sweet candy made from sugar, butter and milk, often flavored with chocolate.
examples: I ate a piece of chocolate fudge.
Mom made fudge for the holiday party.
The ice cream had a swirl of fudge in it.

related.def: Like fudge; soft, sweet and rich.

easy.def: Something that is burned to make heat or power.
examples: The car needs fuel.
Wood is a fuel.
The fuel is gone.

more.def: Something burned to give heat or power, such as gas, wood or coal.
examples: The car ran out of fuel.
Wood is a fuel that people burn in a fireplace.
The rocket carried a lot of fuel.

easy.def: A person who is running away.
examples: The fugitive hid.
The police searched for the fugitive.
The fugitive ran.

more.def: A person who is running away from the police or from danger.
examples: The fugitive crossed the river at night.
The fugitive hid in the woods.
In the story, a fugitive ran from the king.
I fulfilled my promise.
She fulfills her duty.
He fulfilled his dream.

more.def: To carry out a promise or complete something that was needed.
examples: I fulfilled my promise to walk the dog.
She fulfilled her dream of becoming a pilot.
The store fulfilled our order on time.
The cup is full.
My bag is full of books.
The bus is full.

more.def: Holding as much as it can, with no room left.
examples: The stadium was full of cheering fans.
She poured juice until the glass was full.
The bus was so full that some people had to stand.
I am full after lunch.
He ate until he was full.
The cat is full.

more.def: Having eaten so much that you cannot eat any more.
examples: I'm too full to eat any more spaghetti.
The baby was full and pushed the spoon away.
After the big meal, everyone felt full and sleepy.
The cup is fully filled.
I am fully awake.
The tank is fully charged.

more.def: To the greatest degree, with nothing missing.
examples: The cup was fully filled.
I am fully awake now.
The battery is fully charged.
The paint gave off fumes.
I smelled fumes.
The car gave out fumes.

more.def: A strong-smelling gas, smoke or vapor, often harmful.
examples: The paint gave off strong fumes.
Car fumes made the air hard to breathe.
Open the window to let the fumes out.
Dad fumed.
She fumed about the mess.
He fumes when he loses.

more.def: To feel or show great anger.
examples: Dad fumed when he saw the broken window.
She fumed about the mess in the hall.
He fumes silently when he loses a game.
We had fun.
Swimming is fun.
It was a lot of fun.

more.def: Enjoyment, or something that makes you happy and gives you a good time.
examples: We had so much fun at the water park.
The class played games just for fun.
Building a snowman is fun on a cold day.
It was a fun game.
What a fun day!
That is a fun toy.

more.def: Enjoyable and pleasant.
examples: The party was fun, with games and music.
She is a fun friend who always makes me laugh.
We had a fun day at the fair.
The function of a heart is to pump blood.
What is the function of a fork?
A pen's function is to write.

more.def: The special job or purpose that something has.
examples: A hinge's function is to let the door swing open.
What is the function of this button?
A bridge's function is to help people cross water.
The machine does not function.
The radio functions well.
The clock still functions.

more.def: To work in the right way.
examples: The old clock still functions well.
A bike cannot function with a flat tire.
The new machine functions smoothly.
The radio is functional.
A functional tool.
The old car is still functional.

more.def: Able to work properly, or designed to be useful rather than to look fancy.
examples: The old clock is still functional, and it keeps perfect time.
The kitchen is plain but functional, with everything within reach.
We fixed the radio, and now it is functional again.
We raised a fund for the library.
The fund is for new books.
The class made a fund.

more.def: An amount of money that is saved or collected for a certain purpose.
examples: We started a fund to buy books for the library.
The class raised a fund for the animal shelter.
The fund will pay for the new playground.
Reading is a fundamental skill.
Kindness is a fundamental rule.
A fundamental part.

more.def: Forming the basic part of something; very important.
examples: Reading is a fundamental skill for school.
Kindness is a fundamental part of being a good friend.
The fundamental idea of the game is easy to learn.

easy.def: Money given to pay for something.
examples: The school got funding for a new library.
The park needs more funding.
Funding paid for the new swings.

more.def: Money that is given or set aside to pay for a project, a school or an organization.
examples: The town gave funding to build a new playground by the river.
Our class club needed funding to buy paint and brushes.
The zoo used its funding to build a bigger home for the elephants.
The school raised funds.
We collected funds for the shelter.
The funds are in the bank.

more.def: Money that is saved or given for a certain purpose.
examples: The school raised funds for a new playground.
We collected funds for the animal shelter.
The club ran low on funds.

easy.def: A service when someone has died.
examples: We went to a funeral.
The funeral was sad.
People wore black to the funeral.

more.def: A ceremony held after a person dies, to say goodbye.
examples: We went to a funeral for my great-uncle.
Family and friends gathered at the funeral.
The funeral was held in a quiet church.

easy.def: A plant-like living thing, such as a mushroom or mold.
examples: A mushroom is a fungus.
Fungus grows on bread.
The fungus is on the log.

more.def: A living thing that is not a plant or an animal and feeds on dead things, such as a mushroom or mold.
examples: A mushroom is a kind of fungus that grows on the damp forest floor.
Mold on old bread is a fungus.
A fungus grew on the rotting log.
I was in a funk.
He is in a funk.
She got out of her funk.

more.def: A bad mood in which you feel low or sad.
examples: I was in a funk after the rainy weekend.
He sat alone in a funk after losing the game.
A walk in the sun helped her out of her funk.
The joke is funny.
A funny clown.
That was so funny!

more.def: Causing laughter, or amusing.
examples: The clown's funny hat made the whole crowd laugh.
My uncle tells funny stories about his dog.
It was funny when the puppy chased its own tail.
That is a funny noise.
The milk tastes funny.
He has a funny look.

more.def: Strange or unusual in a way that is hard to explain.
examples: The soup has a funny taste.
I heard a funny noise coming from the engine.
It is funny how quiet the house is when everyone is gone.

easy.def: The soft hair that covers an animal.
examples: The cat has soft fur.
The fur is brown.
The rabbit's fur is white.

more.def: The thick, soft hair that covers the bodies of many animals.
examples: The cat's fur is soft and gray.
The bear's thick fur keeps it warm.
I brushed the dog's fur.
Dad was furious when the dog ate the cake.
The furious bee buzzed at us.
Mom was furious about the mud on the rug.

more.def: Extremely angry.
examples: She was furious when she found out someone had broken her model.
The coach was furious when the team skipped practice.
He was furious with himself for losing his new jacket.

easy.def: In a very angry or very fast way.
examples: He wrote furiously.
The bull snorted furiously.
They worked furiously.

more.def: With great anger, or with great speed and effort.
examples: He scribbled furiously to finish the test.
She pedaled furiously to catch the bus.
The wind blew furiously.

easy.def: A machine that heats a building.
examples: The furnace keeps us warm.
Our furnace is in the basement.
The furnace turned on.

more.def: A machine that makes heat to warm a house or building, or a very hot space used for melting metal.
examples: The furnace in the basement warms the whole house in winter.
The workers poured melted iron from the furnace into a mold.
Dad changed the filter on our furnace before the cold weather came.

easy.def: Tables, chairs and beds in a home.
examples: We bought new furniture.
The furniture is wood.
A chair is furniture.

more.def: Things such as chairs, tables and beds that fill a room.
examples: We bought new furniture for the living room.
A sofa and a table are furniture.
The movers carried the furniture upstairs.
The kitten is furry.
A furry coat.
My dog is furry.

more.def: Covered with fur or soft hair, or soft like fur.
examples: The furry puppy rolled around in the grass.
She wore a furry hat to keep her ears warm.
The caterpillar was green and furry.
Do not go further.
The park is further down the road.
He threw the ball further than me.

more.def: At or to a greater distance, or to a greater degree.
examples: The bakery is further down the road.
She threw the ball further than her brother.
We need to study the problem further.
I need further help.
Do you want further directions?
There is no further news.

more.def: More, or extra.
examples: We need further information before we decide.
The teacher gave further directions.
There will be no further delays.
He was filled with fury.
The fury of the storm scared us.
She stomped in fury.

more.def: Very strong anger, or the great force of something such as a storm.
examples: He was red with fury when he saw the broken toy.
The fury of the storm shook the windows.
The wind blew with fury across the open fields.

easy.def: A safety part that stops electricity when there is too much.
examples: The fuse blew.
The fuse is small.
Dad changed the fuse.

more.def: A small safety part that melts and stops the electricity if there is too much.
examples: A blown fuse made the lights go out.
Dad replaced the fuse in the box.
The fuse protects the wires from too much power.

easy.def: Too much worry or excitement about a small thing.
examples: Do not make a fuss.
The baby made a fuss.
There was a fuss.

more.def: A lot of worry, noise or bother about something small.
examples: Do not make such a fuss about a little spill.
The baby made a fuss at bedtime.
There was a fuss over the lost mitten.

easy.def: The time that has not come yet.
examples: In the future, I want to be a vet.
We will have a new school in the future.
No one can see the future.

more.def: The time that is still to come, after now.
examples: No one knows exactly what will happen in the future.
In the future, cars may drive themselves.
She is saving her money for the future.

easy.def: Soft and covered with tiny hairs.
examples: The peach is fuzzy.
I have a fuzzy blanket.
The chick is fuzzy.

more.def: Covered with soft, fluffy hairs, or not clear.
examples: The baby chick was soft and fuzzy.
I wrapped up in a fuzzy blanket.
The picture was fuzzy and hard to see.
